entries.notes: Baseline: clean single total, unambiguous date, no heading collision.
Two differing Total lines -- exercises extractAmount's ambiguity flag.
No total/grand total keyword anywhere -- exercises NO_AMOUNT_FOUND.
No date pattern anywhere -- exercises NO_DATE_FOUND.
First line is a document heading -- exercises MERCHANT_LOOKS_LIKE_HEADING.
No text at all -- exercises NO_TEXT_RECOGNISED (and the amount/date reasons it implies).
Customer name/mobile line redacted (black bar) before committing.
Has both 'Food Total' and 'Total' lines with different values -- real ambiguity case; the last-match selection rule still lands on the correct 525.
Sub Total and Grand Total both present with different values -- grand-total priority should still select 1947 correctly.

KNOWN LIMITATION CANDIDATE: 'Grand Total (Rounded)  202.00' has a parenthetical between the label and the value; extractAmount's [^\d]* skip could plausibly stop early if OCR linearizes text unexpectedly. A mismatch here is a real finding, not a bad ground truth.

KNOWN LIMITATION CANDIDATE: 'GRAND TOTAL (ROUNDED OFF TO 25 PAISE) 50.25' -- the parenthetical note contains digits ('25 PAISE'), which could be captured instead of 50.25 depending on OCR line order. A mismatch here is a real finding, not a bad ground truth.
Marked 'Duplicate' at the top of the receipt; Name field is an unfilled placeholder (M: 0000000000), not real customer data.

KNOWN LIMITATION: the true payable total is only ever labelled 'Gross Amount', which extractAmount's regex does not match at all -- the only 'total'-labelled line is 'Sub Total 699.00' (pre-discount). Expect amountMatch to fail; this is the intended finding, not a bad ground truth -- see corpus/README.md.

KNOWN LIMITATION: the true payable total is only ever labelled 'Bill Amt' (post-GST); the only 'total'-labelled line is 'TOTAL 216.00' (pre-GST). Expect amountMatch to fail; this is the intended finding. Customer name line redacted (black bar) before committing.

KNOWN LIMITATION: date is printed as '12-Sep-2026' (abbreviated month name with hyphens), which extractDate's regex does not match (it expects all-numeric d/m/y or 'D Month YYYY' with whitespace, not hyphens, before a full month name). Expect dateMatch to fail; this is the intended finding. Name field says 'CASH CUSTOMER' (generic, not real).
